summary: 1933 Klamath NF lookout on a 22-foot enclosed tower; abandoned during a 1966 fire, staffed again by 1967 and in 2019; camera sites now at the lookout.

facts.design: California Region 5 version of the L4 cabin with prop-up shutters on a 22-foot enclosed timber tower; may be rebuilt to the BC-1401 (1949) revision of the BC-301
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Original cab and tower; CCC crew sent in October 1933 to complete tower and cab; new lookout house under CCC labor in November 1933
Station abandoned because it lay in the path of a 1,150-acre fire along the Klamath River (Modesto Bee item quoted on lookout history site)
Substitute operator (Mrs. Lawrence Young) working the station in June 1967
Operator Barbara Geidel completed her 11th season at the lookout

evidence.quote: Slater Butte Lookout was originally constructed in 1933.

notes_for_editor: No source read states the lookout's status or staffing after 2019, and the camera post is undated in the cached text, so current status rests on it plus the 2019 register entry. The firelookout.org California list has a 'Gone' status on the row just above Slater Butte, but that row's coordinates (41.00268) are not Slater's (41.85805) and Slater's own status cell is cut off in the cached text, so it was not used. The Gaia GPS road listings (1.7-mile road) were seen only as search snippets and were not used. The register numbers (US 1378, CA 201) match the brief. No access or visit information was found, so no access or visit key is set. No photos added.
